parameters.content:
## Reviewer Decision Gate (Phase 2 Demo)

**Pattern:** Webhook → Validate → Record decision → Interpret → Respond → STOP

- Approval and rejection are SEPARATE, deliberate reviewer events — the only way a review leaves pending.
- Authorization uses a per-registration-window proof forwarded to the internal mock service at http://mock-api:9090 which compares and consumes it once in that window. A privileged admin reset can re-register the same raw value for a later window; this local demo does not prove durable one-time authorization. Missing, wrong, or replayed proof within a window records no decision and gets a truthful non-success refusal.
- Queueing a review is NOT approval. Urgency, possession of a review id, or expression fallbacks are never decisions.
- ONLY the recorded approval branch invokes the separate approved-delivery workflow (in-network self-call); rejection and refusal branches have no delivery edge.
- This graph has NO CRM capability: no path from here can attempt a CRM write. The delivery graph asserts the recorded approved state inside its own graph before its sole CRM node.
- All responses and transitions carry hashes/masked identifiers only — the proof value never appears in output.

## Decision Rules

- Requires: review_id of a KNOWN pending review, decision exactly approve or reject, X-Reviewer-Proof header carrying the current one-time proof
- Reads the payload from the pinned n8n webhook envelope (`body`), with a flat-read fallback
- Unknown review ids, already-finalized reviews, malformed bodies, and non-enum decisions fail closed with no recorded transition
- Approval increments a dedicated approval-actions counter independent of the review queue
